slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
From the Atlantic coast to the central highlands, six Loire sub-regions each write a unique chapter in the world's richest wine story. Pays Nantais' fresh Muscadet, Anjou-Saumur's honeyed sweet wines, Touraine's château country diversity, Centre-Loire's mineral Sauvignon Blanc, Vallée du Loir's northern spice — plus Haut-Poitou, the Loire's boundary-crossing ambassador.

Learning Objectives

🌊 Master Pays Nantais

From basic Muscadet to the top Crus Communaux — all in the same region

🍯 Discover Anjou-Saumur's range

World-class sweet wines alongside the elegant Saumur-Champigny reds

🏯 Explore Touraine's diversity

Vouvray, Chinon, Bourgueil — the greatest concentration of classic Loire styles

⛰️ Understand Centre-Loire's mineral peaks

Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé — the global summit of Sauvignon Blanc

🌿 Meet the northern zones

Vallée du Loir and Haut-Poitou — the Loire's distinctive outliers
slides.1.title: Pays Nantais: The Atlantic Frontier
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Muscadet: The Oyster's Perfect Partner
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Pays Nantais produces one of France's great food wines — Muscadet's high acidity, minerality and saline freshness make it an unrivalled match for oysters and seafood
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Crus Communaux: A New-Generation Classification
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The 10 'Crus Communaux' recognised since 2011 require at least 18 months of sur lie contact — completely overturning the old image of Muscadet as a cheap, simple wine
slides.1.content:
Pays Nantais is the Loire Valley's westernmost sub-region, clustered around the Atlantic city of Nantes. Here, under the influence of the Atlantic, the Melon de Bourgogne grape produces the Loire's most distinctive white wine — Muscadet.

🏆 Key Pays Nantais AOPs

Muscadet Sèvre-et-Maine

The largest and most prestigious Muscadet appellation, home to the Crus Communaux system. Key villages: Clisson, Gorges, Goulaine, Le Pallet

Muscadet Côtes de Grandlieu

A smaller appellation around Lake Grandlieu — fresh, mineral, maritime

Muscadet Coteaux de la Loire

Easternmost Muscadet zone; slightly more structured

Gros Plant du Pays Nantais

Made from Folle Blanche — ultra-high acidity, extremely lean; the ultimate oyster wine

Coteaux d'Ancenis

A small zone producing light reds and whites from Gamay and Malvoisie (Pinot Gris)
slides.1.quiz.question: What is the key difference between Muscadet 'Crus Communaux' and ordinary Muscadet sur lie?
slides.1.quiz.options.0: They use a different grape variety
slides.1.quiz.options.1: Crus Communaux require a minimum of 18–24 months of sur lie contact, giving them far greater ageing potential
slides.1.quiz.options.2: The Crus Communaux zone is larger
slides.1.quiz.options.3: Crus Communaux cannot use Melon de Bourgogne
slides.1.quiz.explanation: The Crus Communaux are Muscadet's premier cru equivalent: recognised since 2011, they require at least 18 months of sur lie contact (with many producers extending this to 3–5 years), compared with just 4 months for ordinary Muscadet sur lie. The extended lees contact builds extraordinary texture, complexity and an ageing potential of 10–15 years — completely overturning the old Muscadet image.
slides.2.title: Anjou-Saumur: Sweet Wine Paradise and Red Wine Treasure
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Anjou: Home to Some of the World's Greatest Sweet Wines
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Coteaux du Layon, Quarts de Chaume Grand Cru, Bonnezeaux — three world-class sweet white AOPs concentrated in a single sub-region
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Saumur: Wine Culture in Tuffeau Caves
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The tuffeau plateau south of Saumur produces Saumur-Champigny (Loire's most acclaimed red) and the traditional-method Crémant de Saumur sparkling wines
slides.2.content:
Anjou-Saumur is one of the Loire Valley's most diverse sub-regions — simultaneously home to some of the world's greatest sweet wines and some of Loire's most celebrated dry reds.

🍯 Sweet Wine Heartland: Anjou

Quarts de Chaume Grand Cru

40 ha; Loire's only Grand Cru sweet wine AOP; schist and tuffeau; ages 30–50+ years

Bonnezeaux

Schist soils; deep, concentrated sweet white; saffron, tropical fruit, dried apricot

Coteaux du Layon

The largest Loire sweet wine zone; botrytis and late harvest; wide range of styles

Savennières

Dry Chenin Blanc on schist; the Loire's greatest dry white; ages 20–30 years

🏰 Tuffeau Culture: Saumur

Saumur-Champigny

100% Cabernet Franc; tuffeau soils; elegant raspberry, silky mineral — Loire reds' most celebrated ambassador

Crémant de Saumur / Saumur Brut

Traditional method sparkling; primary blend of Chenin Blanc; aged in tuffeau cave cellars
slides.2.quiz.question: Which grape variety primarily produces the red wines of Saumur-Champigny AOP?
slides.2.quiz.explanation: Saumur-Champigny is a 100% Cabernet Franc appellation, located on the tuffeau plateau south of Saumur. Its silky texture, raspberry and strawberry aromas and mineral finish make it the Loire's most internationally acclaimed red AOP and are often described as 'the ambassador of Loire reds'.
slides.3.title: Touraine: Wine Diversity in Château Country
slides.3.highlights.0.title: The Wine Heart Around Tours
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Touraine is the Loire Valley's geographic and historic centre; Vouvray, Chinon, Bourgueil and other world-class AOPs are concentrated here
slides.3.highlights.1.title: The Most Diverse Single Sub-Region
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Dry, off-dry, sweet, sparkling whites; light to medium reds; rosés — all styles appear in Touraine
slides.3.content:
Touraine — the Land of Châteaux — is one of the Loire Valley's richest and most diverse sub-regions. From sparkling Vouvray to structured Chinon reds, Touraine presents the full Loire spectrum.

🏯 Key Touraine AOPs

Vouvray

100% Chenin Blanc; dry (sec), off-dry (demi-sec), sweet (moelleux) and sparkling (pétillant/mousseux) — all from the same AOP

Tuffeau soils; ages 10–30 years for the best dry examples

Montlouis-sur-Loire

Vouvray's mirror on the south bank; similar styles in a slightly more accessible expression

Chinon

100% Cabernet Franc; tuffeau plateau + gravel terraces give two quite different styles

Bourgueil / Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil

100% Cabernet Franc; north bank of the Loire; lighter and more approachable than Chinon

Touraine (generic)

Wide range of grapes and styles; best value entry point into the Loire Valley
slides.3.quiz.question: What is one truly distinctive characteristic of Vouvray?
slides.3.quiz.options.1: The same AOP can produce dry, off-dry, sweet or sparkling wine depending on the vintage
slides.3.quiz.options.2: Only red wine is produced; no whites allowed
slides.3.quiz.explanation: Vouvray's most remarkable feature is its 'polymorphism' — the same AOP can produce dry (sec), off-dry (demi-sec), sweet (moelleux) or sparkling (pétillant/mousseux) wines. In warmer vintages, producers make sweet wines; in cooler years, dry whites. This 'dance with the climate' makes Vouvray one of the most fascinating white wine AOPs in the world.
slides.3.quiz.options.3: It is famous for oak-aged wines
slides.4.title: Centre-Loire: The Final Chapter in Minerality
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Sancerre: Sauvignon Blanc's Holy Land
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Three soil types (marl, silex, limestone debris) give Sancerre three distinct style variations, making it the definitive textbook for Sauvignon Blanc; it also produces Pinot Noir reds and rosés
slides.4.highlights.1.title: The Smoky Flint: Pouilly-Fumé's Signature
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Silex soils give Pouilly-Fumé Sauvignon Blanc a uniquely smoky 'pierre à fusil' (gunflint) minerality — the origin of the name 'Fumé' (smoky)
slides.4.content:
Centre-Loire is the Loire Valley's easternmost sub-region — and the one most distinct in character. Here, at the cusp of semi-continental climate, Sauvignon Blanc finds its greatest expression on French soil.

⛰️ Key Centre-Loire AOPs

Sancerre

Three soil types: terres blanches (marl) = complex, age-worthy; silex (flint) = smoky mineral; caillotes (limestone debris) = fresh, fruity, early drinking

Also produces Sancerre Rouge (Pinot Noir) — an elegant, lighter style

Pouilly-Fumé

Flint-dominated soils; the 'gunflint' signature; fuller-bodied than Sancerre; legendary producers include Dagueneau (Baron de L, Silex)

Menetou-Salon

Kimmeridgian marl soils; similar to Sancerre in style but better value; highly recommended

Quincy / Reuilly

Small appellations with Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Gris (Reuilly rosé)

Coteaux du Giennois

Northernmost Centre-Loire appellation; lighter whites and reds
slides.4.quiz.question: What are Sancerre's three main soil types and what are their stylistic signatures?
slides.4.quiz.options.1: Terres blanches/marl (complex, fine, age-worthy), silex/flint (smoky, mineral), caillotes/limestone debris (fresh, fruity)
slides.4.quiz.explanation: Sancerre's three soil types are its most important point of study: 1) Terres blanches (Kimmeridgian marl) — the most complex and age-worthy; 2) Silex (flint) — the smoky, mineral gunflint character; 3) Caillotes (limestone debris) — fresh, vibrant, fruit-forward, for early drinking. Understanding these three explains why wines from different Sancerre producers can vary so dramatically in style.
slides.5.title: Vallée du Loir: A Northern World of Spice
slides.5.highlights.0.title: Homeland of Pineau d'Aunis
slides.5.highlights.0.content: The Loir valley (note: the Loir river, without an 'e', is a Loire tributary) is the ancestral home of Pineau d'Aunis, the Loire's most aromatic native red variety
slides.5.highlights.1.title: The Loire's Coolest Sub-Region
slides.5.highlights.1.content: Due to its position further north, the Vallée du Loir has a cooler climate; Chenin Blanc here is austere and demanding in youth but capable of extraordinary development with age
slides.5.content:
Vallée du Loir is often overlooked, but it is one of the Loire wine world's most fascinating and distinctive zones. The Loir river (a Loire tributary, flowing from north-east to south-west) creates a unique microclimate and a set of wines unlike anything produced further south.

🌿 Vallée du Loir Key AOPs

Jasnières

Variety: 100% Chenin Blanc (white wine only)

Soils: Tuffeau, south-facing slopes

Style: Bone dry, extremely high acidity, strong mineral character; austere in youth but develops extraordinary complexity after 10+ years; one of the Loire's most underrated great whites

Area: Approximately 60 ha — very rare

Coteaux du Loir

Varieties: Chenin Blanc (white); Pineau d'Aunis + Gamay + Cabernet Franc (red/rosé)

Style: Whites are dry and mineral; reds and rosés are dominated by Pineau d'Aunis' distinctive pepper and red fruit character

Coteaux du Vendômois

Varieties: Pineau d'Aunis (red/rosé); Chenin Blanc (white)

Style: Known for Pineau d'Aunis gris (a kind of rosé) with its peppery character; fresh, aromatic, entirely individual
slides.5.quiz.question: Which grape variety makes Jasnières AOP, and what is its character?
slides.5.quiz.options.0: Sauvignon Blanc — herbal freshness, for early drinking
slides.5.quiz.options.1: Chenin Blanc — high acidity, strong mineral character, great ageing potential; one of the Loire's most underrated great whites
slides.5.quiz.options.2: Muscadet/Melon de Bourgogne — light, saline, pairs with seafood
slides.5.quiz.options.3: Pineau d'Aunis — spicy red wine with white pepper character
slides.5.quiz.explanation: Jasnières is a 100% Chenin Blanc white wine AOP, covering approximately 60 ha — one of the Loire's rarest and most northerly great whites. The south-facing tuffeau slopes create wines of extraordinary acidity and mineral depth. Young Jasnières is often austere and closed, but with 10–20 years of ageing it develops layers of honey, beeswax and mineral complexity that collectors prize highly.
slides.6.title: Haut-Poitou: A Special AOP Across Administrative Borders
slides.6.highlights.0.title: A Geographically Unusual Presence
slides.6.highlights.0.content: Haut-Poitou lies in the Vienne département (Nouvelle-Aquitaine region) — administratively outside the Loire Valley, yet included within the Loire wine family by InterLoire
slides.6.highlights.1.title: Where Ocean and Continent Meet
slides.6.highlights.1.content: Haut-Poitou's climate transitions between Atlantic and continental influences; this midpoint creates wines of fresh acidity and bright fruit
slides.6.content:
Haut-Poitou is one of the Loire wine world's most intriguing boundary cases. Located administratively in Nouvelle-Aquitaine (not the Loire region), it is included in the Loire wine family by InterLoire due to the influence of the Vienne river.

📋 Haut-Poitou Key Facts

  • Location: Vienne département, Nouvelle-Aquitaine region
  • AOP granted: 2011 (promoted from VDQS)
  • Soils: Clay-limestone, tuffeau
  • Climate: Between oceanic (Atlantic) and continental; warm summers, relatively dry autumns
  • Key varieties: Sauvignon Blanc (white), Chardonnay (white), Gamay (red), Cabernet Franc (red), Pinot Noir (rosé)

🍷 Wine Style

Haut-Poitou wines are characterised by their freshness and approachability. Sauvignon Blancs are aromatic and crisp; Gamay-based reds are light and fruit-forward. Quality and price are consistently good, making Haut-Poitou an excellent introduction to Loire wine.
slides.6.quiz.question: What is special about Haut-Poitou's administrative and geographic status?
slides.6.quiz.options.0: It is located in the Paris basin and is the Loire's northernmost appellation
slides.6.quiz.options.1: It is administratively part of Nouvelle-Aquitaine (not the Loire region) but is included in the Loire wine family due to the influence of the Vienne river
slides.6.quiz.options.2: It is the only Loire AOP producing only red wine
slides.6.quiz.options.3: It is France's largest AOP by area
slides.6.quiz.explanation: Haut-Poitou's most distinctive feature is its cross-border status: it lies in the Vienne département of Nouvelle-Aquitaine, which is not formally part of the Pays de la Loire administrative region. However, because it falls within the watershed of the Vienne river (a key Loire tributary) and its wines share a stylistic affinity with the Loire, InterLoire officially includes it in the Loire wine family. This makes Haut-Poitou the Loire's most intriguing boundary case.
